newsitem.title: USA: Albright to visit Europe, Asia on inaugural trip.
newsitem.headline: Albright to visit Europe, Asia on inaugural trip.

text.p: New U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright will visit nine European and Asian capitals, including Beijing, this month on her first overseas trip since taking office, the State Department said on Monday.
Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said Albright would go to Rome, Bonn, Paris, Brussels, London, Moscow, Seoul, Tokyo and Beijing on the round-the-world trip from Feb. 15 to 25.

U.S. secretaries of state usually make their first trips to the NATO allies in Europe. But Albright, an expert on Europe, included Asia in a sign of the rising importance the United States gives to that region too, officials said.

Burns said the decision to go to both continents "reflects the fundamental national interest that we have both in Europe, as a European power, and in the Asia Pacific region as an Asian Pacific power".

Speaking at a regular State Department news conference, Burns said the dates of the trip would be Rome on Feb. 15-16, Bonn on Feb. 16-17, Paris on Feb. 17-18, Brussels on Feb. 18, London on Feb. 18-19, Moscow on Feb. 19-21, Seoul on Feb. 22-23, Tokyo on Feb. 23-24 and Beijing on Feb. 24-25.

Albright will be talking to national government leaders in all the capitals she visits except for Brussels, where she will meet NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana and foreign ministers of the Western alliance.

Many of the visits are essentially courtesy calls. But Albright is expected to have important discussions in Moscow on NATO expansion and in Beijing on human rights and a range of other contentious issues.
Absent from Albright's itinerary is any country in the Middle East, a region to which her predecessor, Warren Christopher, devoted many of his foreign trips.
Albright, who was sworn in on Jan. 23, was also scheduled to travel to Houston, Texas, this Friday and Saturday.

There, she will meet Mexican Foreign Minister Jose Angel Gurria, former U.S. President George Bush and former Secretary of State James Baker. She will also deliver a major policy speech at the James A. Baker Institute for Public Policy at Rice University.
